List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Agro and Rural Industries; Atomic Energy; Coal;
Communications and Information Technology; External Affairs; Labour and

Drug research in India
*221. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) what steps his Ministry is taking or
propose to take to focus on drug research
in India;
(b) the money spent on drug research
during the last five years, year-wise;
(c) the money spent on drug research,
percentage-wise, out of profit earned by
companies during the last five years, year-
wise; and
(d) the measures Government are taking
to make India a leader in drug development?
Cellular phone service in the North
Eastern Region
†*222. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a)  the number of districts in the North
Eastern Region which are not having cellular
phone services;
(b) whether Government propose to
provide cellular phone services in such
districts; and
(c) if so, Government's policy in this
regard?
Central Inland Water Transport
Corporation
*223. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
a proposal for revival of the Central Inland
Water Transport Corporation; and
† Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

67
(b) if so, the response of Government
thereto?
Subsidence in Eastern Coal Fields
Limited
*224. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI DIPANKAR
MUKHERJEE:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether there has been serious
subsidence in Sanctoria area of Eastern Coal
Fields Ltd.;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the immediate measures taken, so
far to rehabilitate and compensate the
affected people; and
(d) the short term/long term measures
taken to prevent such subsidence?
Upgradation of highways in Bihar
†*225. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a)  the total length of National
Highways under National Highways
Development Project and Pradhan Mantri
Bharat Jodo Pariyojana respectively in
Bihar which are to be upgraded to four lane,
project-wise;
(b) the extent and the point from which
Patna is proposed to be connected and
joined through four lane National Highways
under Pradhan Mantri Bharat Jodo
Pariyojana; and
(c) the details of the progress of the
scheme?
Overbridge on NH-5
*226. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Road
Safety Forum had demanded a pedestrian
overbridge at Gundugolanu village on
National Highway No. 5;
(b) whether it is a fact that NHAI is
reluctant to receive and entertain
suggestions from road safety experts and
activists; and
(c) the steps proposed to correct this
situation immediately?
Budgetary allocation to States
*227. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Planning Commission
has decided to make additional budgetary
allocations for current fiscal year to the
States;
(b) if so, whether the Commission is
shuffling funds from one head to another
to help hard pressed States;
(c) if so, whether Centrally sponsored
schemes would be provided money from
State share of Rs. 10 crores additional funds
and State share may be squeezed;
(d) if so, the details of funds utilisation
by Planning Commission; and
(e) to what extent this has helped
deserving States to meet their financial
position?
† Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

68
Denial by Pakistan for an extradition
treaty
*228. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
of Pakistan has declined an Indian proposal
for an extradition treaty between the two
countries;
(b) if so, the specific reasons stated by
the Government of Pakistan in regard
thereto; and
(c) Government's reaction in this
regard?
Safety of labour
*229. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN: Will
the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are executing
any programme to create awareness of the
safety of labour at their work place;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the segments identified and funds
allocated for the purpose to Tamil Nadu?
Creation of job opportunities
†*230. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that development
without creating additional job
opportunities would not prove beneficial
for the country;
(b) if so, Government's reaction in this
regard;
(c) whether Government would
consider to bring about changes in the
present industrial policy so as to accord
priority and importance to the creation of
jobs in the future plans of the country; and
(d) if so, the comprehensive details in
this regard?
Under invoicing of Access Deficit
Charge
*231. SHRI NILOTPAL BASU: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have identified a grey market in terms of
under invoicing of Access Deficit Charge
(ADC) payments;
(b) if so, the total billion minutes of
international calls received by different
access providers, company-wise since the
TRAI mandated ADC regime has been put
in place and the corresponding money
received by BSNL on account of this; and
(c) the penalties provided for by the
law against defaulters and action initiated
in the matter?
Loan applications under PMRY in
Uttaranchal
*232. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will
the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of educated persons
in Uttaranchal who have applied for loans
to establish their ventures under Pradhan
Mantri Rojgar Yojana during the last two
years and the number of persons out of
them who have been sanctioned loans;
(b) whether some loan applications
received during these two years under the
said scheme have been rejected; and
(c) if so, the number of rejected
applications and the main reasons therefor?
† Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

69
Productivity of Indian Labour
†*233. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that only 28 per
cent of total labour force of the country is
engaged in production work;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
productivity of country's labourer is low
in comparison to the labourer in developed
countries; and
(c) if so, the details with regard to
productivity of the labourers in our country
and those of America, England, Japan and
China?
Suggestions on NRIs marriage
registration
†*234. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the suggestions given
by the Women Commission to Government
in respect of marriage registration of NRIs
and on other matters alongwith the date
when these suggestions were given;
(b) Government's reaction thereto; and
(c) by when a final decision in this
regard is likely to be taken?
Facilities to Gramin Dak Sevaks
*235. SHRI C. RAMACHAN-
DRAIAH: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFOR-
MATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether three lakh Gramin Dak
Sevaks maintaining communications
services to rural India are being denied all
facilities and benefits despite Supreme
Court's ruling to treat them as holders of
civilian posts;
(b) the details of their pending demands;
and
(c) the reaction of Government thereto?
Recovery of outstanding dues of
MTNL and BSNL
*236. DR. AKHILESH DAS: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the arrears by way of telephone dues
payable by the Central Government and
the State Governments to MTNL and
BSNL as at September end this year;
(b) the steps taken to recover and clear
the dues so far and the success achieved in
such recoveries, indicating the latest balance
of the arrears; and
(c) whether any State Governments
have asked the telephone authorities not to
disconnect the telephones for defaults in
payment; if so, the details in this regard?
Medium of examination for DSPs/
Asstt. Commandants
*237. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the selection
of DSPs/Assistant Commandant etc. for
the para-military forces is being done by
the Union Public Service Commission
during the last few years;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that
the written tests are held only in Hindi and
English; and
(c) whether Government would allow
all the languages listed in the Eighth Schedule
to the Constitution as a medium for these
† Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

70
examinations as in the case of the Civil
Services Examination?
Employment opportunities for
engineers
†*238. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the number
of engineers have increased in the country
during last decade;
(b) if so, the number thereof in 2003 as
compared to 1993;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
employment opportunities for engineers
have been depleting in the country at
present; and
(d) if so, the number of unemployed
engineers out of total number of engineers
at present?
Recovery from RIM for misuse of ILD
calls
*239. SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Department of Telecommunications has set
up vigilance telecom cell in all metro cities
to curb the menace of illegal international
long distance calls; and
(b) whether it is a fact that Telecom
Department proceeded against Reliance
Indian Mobile for the recoveries of the
amount for misuse of ILD as local calls?
Separate telecom sector for Bhadohi
*240. SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Bhadohi, forming an
independent revenue district is still under
the juridiction of Telecom District Varanasi;
(b) whether representations are pending
with the Centre, pleading for a separate
telecom district status for Bhadohi, in view
of it's being main center for carpet
manufacturing and export in India;
(c) whether Bhadohi generates large
telecom revenue through large number of
ISD call traffic and is expected to be
declared as Special Economic Zone; and
(d) if so, whether in view of the present
status as international export center,
Government would consider forming a
separate telecom district for Bhadohi?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 10th December, 2004 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 19, 1926 (Saka)

Total number of questions — 155
Donation for ARIs
1435. SHRI SANJAY NIRUPAM: Will
the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have closed
the donation for the Agro industries;
(b) whether the funds released by
Government are not enough to run these
industries; and
(c) if so, the details about the Agro
industries and the release of funds in the
year 2003-04?
PMRY in Maharashtra
1436. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have recently
reviewed performance of on-going projects
under the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana in
Maharashtra;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether his Ministry have set any
target for generating more employment
opportunities in Maharashtra State under
this scheme; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Preservation of fruits and
vegetables
†1437. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Bhabha
Atomic Research Centre has developed a
technique of long lasting preservation of
fruits, vegetables and cereals; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

316
Threat on National Security due to
mining of mineral sands
1438. SHRI N. K. PREMACHAND-
RAN: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any project is pending with
Government to obtain permission for
mining of mineral sands from the coastal
areas of Kollam or from Alappuzha
districts of Kerala State by any private or
joint venture firms;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government see any threat
on the National Security to allow mining of
mineral sands containing rare earths by
private companies; and
(d) if so, Government’s reaction
thereto?
Storage of radioactive wastes
1439. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
PRIME MINISTER  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that management
and disposal of long-life radioactive wastes
has been a technical and political problem
world-over;
(b) whether it is also a fact that M/s
Reliance Industries Ltd., have released a
comprehensive report to redress this issue;
and
(c) if so, the details thereof especially
those relating to short-term and viable long-
term solution for waste storage?
Private participation in Atomic Energy
production
1440. SHRI K. B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether  the amended Atomic
Energy Act waiting for the approval of the
Parliament provides  for private
participation in nuclear energy production
in the country;
(b) whether according to the amended
provision, the Department of Atomic
Energy and the Nuclear Power Corporation
of  India Limited will be bound to provide
technical support to the private power
producer; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Appointment of UDCs
1441. SHRI VIDYA SAGAR
NISHAD: Will the Minister of ATOMIC
ENERGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that examination
for the post of UDC were held in the month
of June, 2002;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that even
after a lapse of about three years of
examination, selected candidates have not
been called to join ;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(e) by when, the selected candidates
would be called to join?
Setting up of  desalination plant at
Chennai
1442.  SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the PRIME
MINISTER  be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Bhabha  Atomic
Research Centre has worked on
desalination technologies and has
experience in erecting large-scale
desalination plants;
(b) if so, the details of plants erected
by them to help drinking water problem;
and

317
(c) whether they would participate in
the proposed desalination plants to be set
up in Chennai that would produce 300
million litres of potable water a day?
Royalties on coal
1443. SHRI PY ARIMOHAN
MOHAPATRA: Will the Minister of
COAL  be pleased to state:
(a) considering that the ratio between
royalties for higher and inferior rates in coals
as in the year 1971 has progressively
declined against the inferior varieties to
successive revision of royalty whether
Government propose to consider
restoration of the earlier ratio of 1971;
and
(b) if so, within what time-frame  and if
not, the reasons therefor?
Black marketing of coal
1444. SHRI MANOJ
BHATTACHARYA:
DR. ALLADI P.
RAJKUMAR:
 Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether there is a rampant black-
marketing of coal in the market encouraged
by a massive ring of mafia leaders in
connivance with officials of the Coal
Companies and Government;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have analysed
the basic reasons for black-marketing on
such a gigantic scale and  if so, the details
thereof; and
(d) the steps proposed to be taken  in
this regard?
Amendment of the Coal Mines
(Nationalisation) Act
1445. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of COAL
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided not to bring amendment to
Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act to bring
private players into this sector ;
(b) if so, the reasons behind not bringing
an amendment to the above Act as
proposed by previous Government;
(c) by when the Ministry is going to
release mission document for coal 2030;
and
(d) the salient features in the proposed
document?
Loss making units in
coal sector
1446. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will
the Minister of  COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that his Ministry
has proposed a Rs. 6000 crore
rehabilitation fund for Eastern Coalfields,
Bharat cooking Coal  and Central Coalfields;
(b) if so,  the time-frame for
rehabilitation of these units and whether
rehabilitation  would also result in
upgrading the production and productivity
of the labour; and
(c) whether there are any other loss
making units in the coal  sectors and what
is the perspective plan of Government
with regard to such units?

318
Use of surface mining machines by
SECL
†1447. SHRI  RAMADHAR
KASHYAP:  Will the Minister of  COAL
be pleased to state:
(a) the names of locations  in the country
where surface mining machines are used
for coal mining;
(b) the cost  of mining by the surface
mining machines alongwith the cost on
manual mining of the coal;
(c) whether there is any  plan to use
surface mining by SECL;
(d) the reasons for cancellation of
tenders invited for this purpose by SECL
few years ago ; and
(e) the details thereof?
Installation of coal mines safety
devices
1448. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that various
experts have made recommendations to
fulfil and instal numerous coal mine safety
devices and practices in our country;
(b) whether it is a fact that none of these
recommendations have been implemented
in the country;
(c) whether Government are aware of
the  huge loss of human life in periodic coal
mine accidents in the country;
(d) what steps would Government
initiate to instal all such safety devices to
reduce coal mine accidents; and
(e) the specific action proposed in the
next six months by Government in this
regard?
Losses due to non increase of royalty
on coal
†1449. SHRI PY ARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to increase royalty on coal;
(b) whether it is a fact that despite the
increase in prices of coal, States are suffering
heavy losses due to non increase in royalty
to the States;
(c) whether Government have received
any proposal to increase royalty from
Madhya Pradesh Government;
(d) if so, the details of the steps taken
by Government; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Theft of coal from SECL
†1450. SHRI RAMADHAR
KASHYAP: Will the Minister of  COAL
be pleased to state:
(a) whether pilferage worth crores of
rupees of coal in the name of rejected coal
is going on in SECL;
(b) whether this would be brought under
the CBI investigation;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Database and information
networking scheme in Madhya
Pradesh
†1451.SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA : Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

319
of Madhya Pradesh have demanded an
amount of Rs. 55.84 lakhs as Central share
for implementation of Centrally Sponsored
Scheme regarding strengthening of data base
and information networking programme in
Madhya Pradesh; and
(b) if so, by when proposed amount is
likely to be sanctioned and released?
Tax exemption and duty  relaxation
on raw material
1452. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of  COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have set a
target of atleast 200 million  telephones by
2007;
(b) if so, whether Government would
require equipment worth Rs. 1,00,000
crores;
(c) if so, whether his Ministry has
already approached Finance Ministry on
the terms the indigenous manufacturing
sector are facing as the industry has been
demanding tax exemption and duty
relaxation on raw materials and components;
and
(d) if so, to what extent the Finance
Minister has agreed and by when
Government are likely to start taking action
for improving telephones as suggested by
the Ministry to achieve it by 2007?
Demand of postal employees
1453.  SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the All India Postal Extra
Department Employees Union has decided
to go on an indefinite strike in support of
its demand for merger of 50  per cent
Dearness Allowance with pay, grant of
trade union facilities and pension;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action taken by Government to
look into their demands?
Conversion of vacant looking
post offices into shopping
areas
1454. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the action taken to modernize the
Indian Post Offices to combat the hi-tech
invasion;
(b) whether Government proposed to
transform the vacant looking post offices
into shopping areas; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Downfall of BPO Sector
1455. SHRI SANJAY NIRUPAM:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have noticed
the future downfall of the BPO Sector;
(b) whether the U.S. stands about the
outsourcing issue has any impact upon the
Indian IT Sector;
(c) whether the India's most employed
youth in IT Sector would have to lose their
job in future; and
(d) Government’s stand in the matter?

320
Retired Telecom Officers working
with Reliance Infocom
1456. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether in the wake of discovery of
the gray international call racket,
Government have set up a Vigilance Squad
to monitor international calls round-the-
clock;
(b) whether the Vigilance Squad has
focused on the suspected involvement of
former telecom officers now working with
the Reliance Infocom;
(c) whether the suspected officials of
Telecom Department had secured
Government's permission, after retirement
to join Reliance Infocom; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Demand of private telecom
operators
1457. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Access Deficit Charge
regime, supposed to provide support for
rural telecom is fraught with regulatory,
legal and procedural short-comings;
(b) whether the Universal Service Fund,
operational from 2002, is adequate to
provide support for the rural telecom
expansion;
(c) whether the private telecom
operators are opposing the ADC regime
and demanding its abolition; and
(d) if so, Government's views thereon?
Malfunctioning of exchanges in
BSNL areas
1458. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there have been complaints
of malfunctioning of the exchanges in BSNL
areas whereby local calls of 3 minute
duration get snapped after 10-20 seconds
due to technical fault;
(b) if so, whether the local customer
entitled to get 3 minute talk time for local
calls has to make many calls aggregating 3
minute duration and pay multiple call
charges instead of single local call; and
(c) if so, the steps being taken to rectify
the system to ensure full utilization of call
time?
Opening of Post Offices in Gram
Panchayat villages
†1459. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the total
number of Gram Panchayat villages without
any post office is 1,15,605 in the country
which is about 49.35 per cent of the Gram
Panchayat villages in the country; and
(b) if so, whether Government propose
to open and provide post offices in all such
Gram Panchayat villages in the country
where there are no post offices and by
when?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

321
Benefit of I.T. to rural
areas
†1460. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any scheme to
formulate plan to provide benefit of
information technology to rural areas;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government are aware of
the fact that because more than 90 per cent
of population of the country is not
conversant with English so they can be
provided the benefit of information
technology either in Hindi or other regional
languages; and
(d) if so, keeping in view the above fact,
what steps have been taken by Government
for development, promotion and
propagation of information technology
through Hindi?
